clue.text: Soldier gets pay for work, others may get it without work

definitions.text: others may get it without work

parts.note: a private is the lowest-ranking soldier
income is money earned for work

explanation.surface: A soldier draws wages for his labour, while others are paid for doing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays one kind of income against another: a soldier's earned pay versus money that arrives without work.
explanation.definitionFit: Unearned money from investments or inheritance, received without having to labour for it.

clue.text: Object when put into torn clothing

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, as the wording says

parts.note: a rent is a tear, so torn gives the noun
an aim is an object or goal

explanation.surface: An item gets thrust into ripped clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn' gives RENT (a tear), and 'Object' is the noun meaning aim, not the verb meaning protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for garments or attire.

clue.text: It turns to face the incoming blow

definitions.text: It turns to face the incoming blow

parts.words: It turns to face the incoming blow
parts.note: reads like a boxer squaring up, but describes a rooftop wind pointer swinging round into the breeze

explanation.surface: A fighter pivots to meet a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather vane rotates on its spindle so that it points into the oncoming wind.

clue.text: It's old news

parts.note: suggests stale gossip, but means an old-fashioned word for news

explanation.surface: Something everybody already knows.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidings is an archaic or literary term for news or information.

clue.text: I'm the type to stamp something out

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
print is printed type

explanation.surface: A person boasts of being the sort to eradicate something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stamp something out' suggests eradicating, but here it means pressing a mark out onto a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To imprint is to press or stamp a mark onto a surface.

clue.text: One possibly in the lead as a conductor

definitions.text: One possibly in the lead as a conductor

parts.words: One possibly in the lead as a conductor
parts.note: suggests a leading orchestral maestro, but describes the conducting wire inside an electric lead

explanation.surface: A maestro who may be at the front of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: The conducting wire at the centre of an electrical cable is called its core.

clue.text: I object to a certain extent

parts.note: me is the object form of the pronoun I
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone raises a partial protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I object' reads as a protest but is grammar: ME is the objective case of I.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure is an amount or degree, as in 'in some measure'.

clue.text: Complaint made by a tiresome person

definitions.meaning: a stiff, aching neck is a physical ailment

explanation.surface: A grumble voiced by a bore.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a literal ache in the neck and, idiomatically, an annoying nuisance.

clue.text: Separate complaints department

parts.note: sounds like a customer-service office, but means a hospital unit keeping infectious illnesses apart

explanation.surface: A distinct office handling customer grievances.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital unit where patients with contagious diseases are kept apart from others.

clue.text: Crooked dealing straightened out

indicators.note: bent out of shape, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Dishonest business has been set right.
explanation.definitionFit: Aligned means brought into a straight line, set in order.

clue.text: Has prep to revise, maybe

indicators.note: revising reworks something, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pupil possibly has homework to go over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prep' is British school slang for homework.
explanation.definitionFit: Perhaps and maybe are both adverbs of possibility.

clue.text: A state that requires relief

parts.note: suggests a country ... aid, but describes a condition of want

explanation.surface: A nation appealing for aid.
explanation.definitionFit: Need is a condition of poverty or lack that calls for help.

clue.text: Open closed teeth

parts.note: sounds like prising apart a clenched jaw, but means parting the interlocked teeth of a fastener

explanation.surface: Prise apart clenched jaws.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening a zip fastener separates its meshed teeth.

clue.text: Dog left to play with stones on the ice

definitions.text: play with stones on the ice

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A dog is left to romp among the rocks on a frozen pond.
explanation.walkthrough: Curling is a sport where granite stones are slid along ice towards a target.
explanation.definitionFit: To curl is to take part in the sport of curling, sliding granite stones on ice.

clue.text: Fight waste!

explanation.surface: A rallying call against wastefulness.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap is both a brawl and leftover junk material.

clue.text: Junk food

definitions.meaning: the edible stomach lining of cattle

explanation.surface: Unhealthy fast food.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe means both nonsense and cow's stomach lining eaten as food.

clue.text: Section reserved for reviews

indicators.note: read as re-served, served up again in a different order

explanation.surface: A part of the paper set aside for critics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserved' looks like booked, but is read as re-served: the letters dished out afresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Notices are critics' published write-ups of plays, films or books.

clue.text: People in the wrong can cause distress

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men means people

explanation.surface: Those who are mistaken can upset others.
explanation.walkthrough: A tort is a legal term for a civil wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To torment is to inflict suffering or anguish on someone.

clue.text: US city entered in a huge novel conveyance

indicators.note: new, so the letters take a fresh order

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: An American city features in a vast book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' turns A HUGE into HAUGE, which LA enters.
explanation.definitionFit: Haulage is the transporting of goods by road.

clue.text: English capital put into new ground and stand

indicators.note: one piece is placed within another
makes fresh, so the letters are rearranged
the capital letter here is the initial one

explanation.surface: An English capital city is built on fresh land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges GROUND into UNDRGO, into which E goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo is to endure or bear something, as stand can mean tolerate.

clue.text: Baltic country resort one is at

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning sort again, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A holiday spot in a northern European nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but signals sorting again.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a nation on the Baltic Sea.

clue.text: A highly vocal female

parts.note: suggests a loud, opinionated woman, but means a singer with the highest voice

explanation.surface: A very outspoken woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest singing voice, usually female.

clue.text: Various chaps in vegetable production

indicators.note: suggests different arrangements of the letters

explanation.surface: Several men grow greens.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green vegetable.

clue.text: Possibly train as a mechanic

indicators.note: says the letters may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Someone might train to become a mechanic.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker, as a mechanic is.

clue.text: Having nothing on dark horse, back favourite finally

indicators.note: betting sense hides a turnaround of the preceding piece

parts.note: a dun is a dull greyish-brown horse

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the closing letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A gambler with no other bets backs an outsider and then the favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like placing a bet on the horse, but it turns the horse round; a dun is a greyish-brown horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Nude means unclothed, wearing nothing.

clue.text: Most airlines can provide this flight

indicators.note: the letters are supplied within the words themselves

explanation.surface: Most carriers can offer this journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' looks like an air trip but means a set of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair is a set of steps, as in a flight of stairs.

clue.text: Wild West dish of meat and vegetables

indicators.note: unruly, so the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A cowboy meal from the Wild West.
explanation.definitionFit: A stew is slow-cooked meat and vegetables in liquid.

clue.text: Post of bodyguard

definitions.meaning: protective armour made of linked rings

explanation.surface: A position as a bodyguard.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail is both letters sent and chain armour guarding the body.

clue.text: Mark some golfer's cards

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Grade some golfers' scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a mark left on the skin by a healed wound.

clue.text: Brief article favoured hanging

parts.note: curt means brief or terse
a is the indefinite article
in means popular or favoured

explanation.surface: A short piece supported execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanging' suggests execution but is a drape hung at a window.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtain is fabric hung at a window, a hanging.

clue.text: He charges a couple of hundred to employer

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two make CC
a user is one who employs something

explanation.surface: A person bills an employer a couple of hundred pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employer' means one who employs a thing, a user, not a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: An accuser is one who brings charges against someone.

clue.text: Inattention may result in her going to law

indicators.note: the letters may produce something new when rearranged

explanation.surface: Not paying attention could see a woman taken to court.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolgathering is idle daydreaming, a lack of attention.
